newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea jails novelist for illegal visit to North.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea jails novelist for illegal visit to North.

text.p: A Seoul court on Tuesday sentenced a South Korean novelist to 3-1/2 years in jail for illegally visiting North Korea and revealing state secrets, a court official said.

Kim Yong, known as his pen name Kim Hah-ki in South Korea, was found guilty of "revealing national secrets during (questioning) by North Korean authorities after illegally entering North Korea", he said.
No details were given of what secrets Kim passed on to the communist North, arch rival of the South.

The novelist, who was held in North Korea for two weeks for a border violation, was arrested on his return home last August on charges of visiting the North on his own will without seeking approval from the Seoul government.
South Korea's National Security Law bans all unauthorised contacts with the North.
North and South Korea are still technically at war since their 1950-1953 conflict ended with a truce, not a peace treaty.
